senses.gloss:
Ātreya
(‘descendant of अत्रि’)
------------------------------------------
Derived from the word ‘Atri,’ the term ‘Ātreya’ can refer to anyone who is a descendant of the sage अत्रि. There are several sages that bear this name. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (8.22) mentions one sage Udamaya, an आत्रेय, as a priest of the king अङ्ग Vairocana. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (2.6.3; 4.6.3) has included the name of one आत्रेय, a disciple of Māṇṭi, as one of the teachers of Madhuvidyā. In the Mahābhārata we come across an आत्रेय who was a disciple of the sage वामदेव. He acted as one of the priests in the सर्पयाग conducted by जनमेजय. It was he who taught spiritual wisdom to विदुर.
Ātreya पुनर्वसु is one of the earliest and well-known teachers of आयुर्वेद (science of longevity). He has sometimes been identified with सुश्रुत.
Ātreya Rāmānuja (A. D. 1220-1295), also known as Kiḍāmbi Appuḷḷār, is an important teacher of the Viśiṣṭādvaita school of Vedānta. He imbibed both the Sanskrit and the Tamil traditions of the school and taught them to his nephew, वेदान्त देशिक (A. D. 1268-1369) another doyen of this school. He was well-versed in the Mīmāṁsā as well as the Vedānta systems of philosophy. Nyāyakuliśa, is his magnum opus. Other works attributed to him are: Divyasūriprabhavadīpikā, Sarva-दर्शन-śiromaṇi and Mokṣasiddhi.

Atri
------------------------------------------
Atri is a well-known ṛṣi or sage often mentioned in the sacred literature of the Hindus. The fifth मण्डल of the Ṛgveda Saṁhitā mentions अत्रि and Ātreyas (descendants of अत्रि) as the ṛṣis through whom it was revealed. His name occurs in other places also (ibid 10.137.4).
Atri is one of the ten मिन्द्-born sons (‘mānasaputras’) of ब्रह्मा the Creator, and classified as a ‘maharṣi’ (great sage). Hence he is one of the Prajāpatis or progenitors of mankind too. He is said to have protected the sun against the एच्लिप्से-demon, Svarbhānu, (the राहु of post-Vedic म्य्थोलोग्य्) by composing a ‘Fourth’ prayer, the other three being the usual liturgy of prayers against an एच्लिप्से. He is also said to have been the पुरोहित or priest of the pañcajanas (five clans or tribes of the Vedic आर्यन्स्). He was tortured by the असुरस् (demons) but protected and rescued by the अश्विन्स् (the twin deities).
He is listed among the सप्तर्षिस् or the Seven Sages. Astral myths refer to him as one of the स्तर्स् of the Saptarṣimaṇḍala or the constellation of the Great Bear.
Atri’s wife was अनसूया (lit., ‘one who has no jealousy’), the daughter of कर्दम प्रजापति. She was the paragon of wifely virtues and chastity. Pleased by the austerities of अत्रि, ब्रह्मा, विष्णु and शिव were born in अनसूया as अत्रि’s sons: चन्द्र, Datta or दत्तात्रेय and दुर्वासस्.
Rāma, while living in the forest दण्डक, visited his hermitage and learnt about the secrets of धर्म (Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇyakāṇḍa, 117) from him.
Ancient writers on धर्मशास्त्रस् have held अत्रि in high esteem. Manusmṛti (3.16) and Mahābhārata (Anuśāsanaparva 65.1) have quoted his views. There is an Ātreya Dharmaśāstra attributed to him. It is in nine chapters and treats of दान (gifts), japya (prayers) and तपस् (austerities).
There are several other works styled ‘Atri स्मृति’ or ‘Atri Saṁhitā’ in manuscripts. One Atri Saṁhitā now available in print, contains 400 verses and deals with most of the topics generally dealt with in the धर्मशास्त्रस्.
See also ANASŪYĀ, DATTĀTREYA and DURVĀSAS.
